clue.text: Oratorio role? Singer out, injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A soloist is dropped from an oratorio because of an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's The Dream of Gerontius is the oratorio; the question mark admits the definition names one role rather than describing a kind of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerontius is the dying old man whose soul's journey is sung by the tenor soloist in Elgar's choral work.

clue.text: Successful student accepting new piano

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the student word holds the following letter

blocks.note: a grad is someone who has graduated

explanation.surface: A graduate takes delivery of a new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside GRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is a large concert piano with horizontal strings, short for grand piano.

clue.text: Ridicule passion tailing off

indicators.note: tailing off means losing the tail, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Mockery takes the heat out of a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: RAGE without its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is British informal for teasing or making fun of them.

clue.text: Very small canal one’s redirected

indicators.note: redirected means sent a different way, so these letters take a new route into order

blocks.note: the nine letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A tiny waterway has had its course changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanoscale describes things measured in billionths of a metre, the realm of molecules and atoms.

clue.text: Hold I uncovered, filled with chlorine

indicators.note: something filled with an item has it inside, so the element symbol goes within

explanation.surface: An uncovered vessel is held and filled with chlorine.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something is to contain it as part of a whole, just as to hold means to contain.

clue.text: Almost brilliant, barbed comment in party

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: a dig is a pointed remark

explanation.surface: A near-perfect put-down delivered at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively celebration or social gathering.

clue.text: Support innovator? One’s bailed

indicators.note: to bail is to get out in a hurry, so the word for one leaves the longer word

blocks.note: a pioneer is the first to try something new

explanation.surface: An inventor's firm has been rescued by a bailout, or one of its people has jumped ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ONE out of PIONEER and PI + ER close up to PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is an upright column or pillar that bears the weight of a bridge or arch, so it holds things up.

clue.text: Stewed prune option is badly timed

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down and broken up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: Offering stewed prunes on the menu comes at the wrong moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inopportune means occurring at an inconvenient or unsuitable moment, which is what badly timed means.

clue.text: Tory shade to make Labour yell, not Liberal, sadly

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is removed
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters left are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Conservative colour makes Labour supporters scream, with no Liberal involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one L from LABOUR YELL and rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep bright blue, the traditional colour of Britain's Conservative Party.

clue.text: Spanish painter having year in old Portuguese territory

indicators.note: having means holding, so the territory word holds the letter inside

blocks.note: Goa in India was a Portuguese colony until 1961

explanation.surface: A Spanish artist spends a year in a former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes inside GOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish court artist of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Technical language deprived of first element

indicators.note: deprived of first means the opening letter of the jargon word is taken away

blocks.note: jargon is the specialist vocabulary of a trade

explanation.surface: Specialist talk stripped of its most basic building block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First element' reads as one phrase, but 'element' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, the inert noble gas with atomic number eighteen found in air.

clue.text: Cross, with overdose appearing in substandard medical treatment

indicators.note: something appearing in another thing shows up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross, X
ropy is British slang for poor quality

explanation.surface: An angry patient complains of an overdose given during poor hospital care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an angry adjective; it is the Greek letter shaped like X. Ropy is informal British for shoddy or unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiropody is the branch of healthcare that treats feet, now often called podiatry.

clue.text: Children avoid being corralled by father or dog

indicators.note: corralled means penned in, so the earlier words end up enclosed by the later one

blocks.note: ch. is the dictionary abbreviation for children
to shun is to keep away from

explanation.surface: Kids try to dodge being rounded up by their dad or the family pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund is a long-bodied, short-legged German breed originally bred to hunt badgers.

clue.text: I’m involved with orchestra … for Beethoven’s Ninth, say?

definitions.text: I’m involved with orchestra … for Beethoven’s Ninth, say?

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A musician says they are taking part in a performance of the Choral Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: someone who could say this of Beethoven's Ninth is the person training its singers.
explanation.definitionFit: A choirmaster trains and conducts a choir, needed for the Ninth Symphony's choral finale, the Ode to Joy.

clue.text: Shock referral to higher court after European withdraws

indicators.note: when someone withdraws they leave, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: an appeal takes a case up to a superior court

explanation.surface: A legal case goes to a higher court with a shocking result once a European party drops out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from APPEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay someone greatly, which is what a shock does.

clue.text: Hard work to include a line in vocal music

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the work word holds the following letters

blocks.note: a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: Learning a single line of a sung piece turns out to be hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: A + L go inside CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a hymn tune of the Lutheran church, sung by choir or congregation.

clue.text: Charlie remains with sum of money, hanging around popular place to pay

indicators.note: hanging around something surrounds it, so the money word goes outside the next word

blocks.note: ash is what is left after burning
a pot is a pool of money

explanation.surface: Someone loiters with leftover cash near a popular checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is from the machine's side: it is where your account pays out to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashpoint is a British term for an automated teller machine where your bank account pays out banknotes.

clue.text: New period in support, backing military chief

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the support word
backing means going in reverse, so the support word is read from its end

blocks.note: an era is a span of time
a leg holds up a table or chair

explanation.surface: A fresh era begins with backing for the army's commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as support for the general, but it only turns the support word round before the other pieces go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a senior army officer commanding large formations, so a chief of the military.

clue.text: Statement of inevitability … which applies to wine-making?

blocks.note: first meaning: a saying that one has to do something whether one likes it or not
second meaning, read literally: wine production cannot happen without pressed grape juice

explanation.walkthrough: Must is the unfermented juice of crushed grapes, so making wine literally requires it.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'needs must when the devil drives' means circumstances compel us, so it states inevitability.

clue.text: Medic definitely keeping head of Government working

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
keeping means holding on to, so one word goes around the other letter

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A doctor is certain the leader of the government is still at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor qualified to perform operations, one kind of medical practitioner.

clue.text: Overlook name of chosen person? Good to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so this letter goes inside the chosen word

explanation.surface: A committee forgets the name of its chosen candidate until someone helpfully steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: N, then G inside ELECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to attend to it, much as overlooking means failing to notice.

clue.text: Piano recital’s opening – avoid piece by Chopin?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pianist begins a recital, perhaps skipping a Chopin piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Chopin wrote a famous set of twenty-four of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin's 24 Preludes, Op. 28, are short piano works, one in every key, so a prelude is an example.

clue.text: Trophies lifted after low point in motor-racing activity

indicators.note: lifted means raised up, and in a down clue that reads the trophy word from the bottom

blocks.note: pots is slang for trophy cups

explanation.surface: A racing team lifts silverware after hitting rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT, then POTS turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is when a racing car halts in the pits for fuel, tyres or repairs mid-race.

clue.text: Like material in bog, a sort that’s recycled

indicators.note: something recycled is broken down and remade, so these letters are reformed in a new order

blocks.note: a type is a sort or kind; these letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: Describing the stuff found in a marsh, a kind of matter that breaks down and gets reused.
explanation.walkthrough: Translate 'a sort' as A TYPE before rearranging: the anagram works on the synonym, not the clue's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaty means resembling or containing peat, the decayed plant matter that builds up in waterlogged bogs.

clue.text: US university setback after Democrat failed to turn up

indicators.note: someone who failed to appear is absent, so that letter goes missing
turn up in a down clue means the letters are flipped to read upwards

explanation.surface: An American college has a setback when a Democrat does not show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' seems to finish the story of the absent Democrat, but it also flips what is left. Remove D from DELAY, then read ELAY upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is the Ivy League university in New Haven, Connecticut, founded in 1701.

clue.text: Spectators pour forth around a Northern town

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the second word wraps the single letter

blocks.note: a gate is the number of people attending a match
to shed is to let fall or emit

explanation.surface: A crowd streams out of a ground in a town in the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: A gate is the attendance at a sports match, the number of spectators through the turnstiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town in Tyne and Wear in north-east England, across the river from Newcastle.

clue.text: Enthusiast‘s note upholding protest

indicators.note: to uphold is to hold up from beneath, so in a down clue the note sits below the protest word

explanation.surface: A keen campaigner's note in support of a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upholding' sounds like support for the cause, but in a down entry it is about position: the note goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an informal term for someone who does something with great energy, as in a demon for work.

clue.text: Direct City to invest in international brainpower

indicators.note: to invest in a place is to put something into it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: to tell someone to do something is to direct them
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: An order goes to the City to put money into global brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' sounds financial, fitting the City, but it only means putting inside. The City, capitalised, is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning and understanding, the mental capacity that brainpower names.

clue.text: Leaders of union now duly ask miners to suspend stoppage

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their front

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Trade union bosses politely ask the miners to call off a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoppage' looks like an industrial strike, but here it is a blockage in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To undam is to remove a dam, so the flow of water that was held back can run again.

clue.text: Chamber group: forte initially cut, then raised

indicators.note: initially cut means the opening letter is chopped off
raised in a down clue means the letters now read upwards

blocks.note: forte is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A chamber ensemble's loud passage is trimmed at the start, then played up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forte' looks like a direct musical instruction but must be translated before cutting: LOUD loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of performers, the smallest ensemble in chamber music, playing together.

clue.text: Benefit I ignored when turning over soil

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped
turning over flips the order, so the remaining letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the fruits of something are its rewards

explanation.surface: A gardener sees no reward in digging over the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from FRUIT, then read FRUT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is the top layer of earth with grass and roots, cut and lifted as sods.

clue.text: Suggestion one day in city will show rain

indicators.note: in puts the day letter inside the city word

blocks.note: a tip is a hint or piece of advice
a town or city, a built-up place

explanation.surface: A weather tip suggests that one day the city will see showers.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip it down is British informal for to pour heavily, a downpour of rain.
